signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (Narodna banka Srbije)
signals.signal: NBS published an OPEN tender (ref JN 201/2026, tender id 378545) for maintenance of the automatic banknote-processing system 'Glory UW-F4', open procedure, CPV 50800000 (miscellaneous repair and maintenance services), notice published 29/07/2026, bid deadline 28/08/2026 09:30. No estimated value is disclosed on the portal. This is plan line 0201 of the NBS 2026 procurement plan (Q2) now converted into a live RFP.
signals.implies: Live cash-automation service contract at a central bank: direct fit for Printec managed services / cash-automation maintenance, and a route into the NBS cash-processing estate (Glory + Giesecke+Devrient installed base).
signals.likelihood: Award expected Q4 2026; single-lot service contract
signals.followup: Download the tender documentation from the portal before 28/08/2026; check whether OEM-authorised-service clauses lock out non-Glory partners.

signals.signal: NBS 2026 procurement plan version 8 (adopted 22/07/2026, published 23/07/2026) still carries line 0003 'Nabavka stonih masina za brojanje i sortiranje novcanica' (purchase of desktop banknote counting and sorting machines), open procedure, CPV 30132200, timing Q2 2026, no estimated value stated. As of 01/08/2026 NO corresponding RFP has been published: a portal search of all NBS procedures returns no reference 'JN 3/2026'.
signals.source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (UJN) – NBS 2026 procurement plan, version 8 (xlsx 'Izmenjena verzija plana nabavki')
signals.implies: Desktop banknote counters/sorters remain an unfilled 2026 opening for Printec cash-automation hardware; the Q2 slot has slipped, so the RFP is most likely H2 2026.
signals.likelihood: RFP plausible in Q3-Q4 2026; already one quarter late
signals.followup: Set a portal subscription on NBS (CAId 3655) CPV 30132200; re-check monthly for reference JN 3/2026.

signals.signal: Plan line 0131 'Masina za brojanje i pakovanje kovanica sa jednim tunelom' (single-tunnel coin counting and packaging machine), CPV 42990000, Q1 2026, exists only as a PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE (Prethodno obavestenje, tender id 347749, ref JN 131/2026, published 06/02/2026) with no deadline and no value; no contract notice has followed as of 01/08/2026. Correction to earlier assumptions: plan line 0132 is NOT coin packaging - it is 'Reducir masina' (a reducing/engraving machine for coin die production, tender id 347753, also prior-information only).
signals.source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (UJN) – NBS prior information notice JN 131/2026 and 2026 plan v8
signals.implies: Coin handling automation at NBS is still pre-tender; a single machine, so a small but defensible hardware sale for Printec cash-automation. The 0132 line is minting equipment, out of Printec scope.
signals.likelihood: RFP possible H2 2026; Q1 target already missed by two quarters
signals.followup: Monitor for reference JN 131/2026 converting to an 'Otvoreni postupak'; brief the coin-handling OEM partner now.

signals.signal: Plan line 0236 of the NBS 2026 plan is a SERVICES line, '„HSM“ uredjaji' (HSM devices), CPV 50530000 (repair and maintenance of machinery), timing Q1 2026, nationwide (RS). As of 01/08/2026 it has NOT been published as an RFP - a portal search of all NBS procedures returns no reference 'JN 236/2026', and no HSM notice appears among the 149 NBS procedures published since 01/01/2026.
signals.source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (UJN) – NBS 2026 procurement plan v8 + NBS procedure list
signals.implies: HSM (hardware security module - the tamper-proof box that holds payment cryptographic keys) maintenance at NBS is an open, still-unlet 2026 line: direct Printec HSM/security and managed-services fit.
signals.likelihood: Two quarters late; RFP plausible H2 2026 or roll-over into the 2027 plan
signals.followup: Approach NBS IT security ahead of the RFP; confirm the installed HSM brand (Thales is used for DinaCard crypto) to size the service scope.

signals.signal: Previously unreported NBS 2026 plan lines with direct Printec relevance, ALL still unpublished as RFPs on 01/08/2026 (no matching reference numbers exist on the portal): 0034 'POS Terminali' (POS terminals, open procedure, Q1); 0030 upgrade of the STIP software module of the Cortex system supporting DinaCard-CUP chip payment cards (CPV 48810000, Q1); 0197 software adaptation on money-counting machines (Q1); 0198 software adaptation on the 'Glory' banknote-processing system (Q1); 0199 dismantling/assembly and relocation preparation of the 'BPS M7' banknote-processing system (Q1); 0200 spare parts and technical support for automatic banknote-processing systems (negotiated procedure without publication, Q1); 0234 vault-equipment maintenance (Q1).
signals.source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (UJN) – NBS 2026 procurement plan v8, lines 0030/0034/0197/0198/0199/0200/0234
signals.implies: A whole unlet pipeline across Printec's core lines: POS terminals, card-switch/issuing software (Cortex/DinaCard), cash-automation software and relocation services, and vault services. Line 0200 is flagged as negotiated-without-publication, i.e. it will go to the incumbent OEM unless challenged early.
signals.likelihood: Several of these should surface as RFPs in H2 2026; line 0200 will likely be a direct award
signals.followup: Pre-position on 0034 (POS) and 0030 (Cortex/DinaCard) now, before specs are frozen; ask NBS whether 0200 will again be a negotiated award.

signals.likelihood: Recurs annually as a direct award
signals.followup: Track the 2027 plan for the equivalent of line 0200; test whether spare-parts supply can be unbundled from OEM support.

signals.signal: NBS published an OPEN tender (ref JN 396/2026, tender id 381910) for 'Izrada i integracija sistema za automatsko sortiranje i kontrolu akciznih markica' (build and integration of a system for automatic sorting and control of excise stamps), CPV 42991000, notice published 24/07/2026, bid deadline 24/08/2026 10:00. signals.signal: Confirmed by direct fetch of the bank's own procurement page (desktop User-Agent defeats the earlier block): the bank states it is NOT subject to the Public Procurement Law and runs procurement under its own internal rules on its website only - and a portal search returns ZERO tenders with Postanska stedionica as contracting authority. Its combined CIT + ATM-servicing tender, 'Nabavka usluge vrsenja poslova pratnje i obezbedjenja transporta i prenosa novca, vrednosnih i drugih posiljaka Banke i usluge opsluge bankomata Banke', bid deadline 30/04/2026, is STILL shown as status 'U toku' (in progress / not yet awarded) as of 01/08/2026. Newer open items on the same page: 'Nabavka storidza za potrebe glavnog bankarskog sistema i aplikacija' (storage for the core banking system, published 08/07/2026, deadline 22/07/2026) and 'Nabavka resenja za kontrolu pristupa i unapredjenje sistema tehnicke zastite' (access control / technical protection upgrade, published 01/07/2026, deadline 14/07/2026).
signals.source_name: Banka Postanska stedionica – Nabavke (own procurement page)
signals.implies: The ATM-servicing half of the CIT award is still winnable/contestable three months after bid close - the single most actionable ATM managed-services opening in Serbia for Printec. It also confirms Serbian commercial banks will never appear on jnportal, so bank-owned pages are the only route.
signals.likelihood: Award decision overdue; announcement plausible within weeks
signals.followup: Contact the bank's procurement office for the award status and the incumbent's identity; register for its bidder notifications so the next ATM-servicing round is caught at publication.

signals.signal: Postanska stedionica is winning Serbian public-sector card-acceptance business: it took the Treasury Administration's 'Usluge platnog prometa preko POS terminala za platne kartice' (ref OP 1/2026, id 348384) with a contract dated 27/02/2026 worth RSD 12,000,000, and JKP for Public Garages and Parking Belgrade's 'Provizija za placanje POS terminalima' (ref JN-17-U/26, id 356177), contract 30/04/2026, RSD 60,000,000. Separately, Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd took the same parking utility's online card-acceptance contract (id 373130, award decision 09/07/2026) after an earlier attempt (id 365865) was discontinued.
signals.source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (UJN) – contracts OP 1/2026 and JN-17-U/26; award decision id 373130
signals.implies: Public-sector acquiring in Serbia is consolidating around Postanska stedionica and Banca Intesa. Both are acquirer accounts rather than competitors for Printec - they are the buyers of POS estates, terminal management and merchant-onboarding platforms.
signals.followup: Target Postanska stedionica and Banca Intesa acquiring teams with terminal-management / POS-estate managed services rather than bidding the utility tenders directly.

signals.signal: Exhaustive keyword and CPV sweeps of the whole Serbian public-procurement portal (751,942 notices, 270,521 procedures, 395,201 contracts indexed as at 01/08/2026) returned ZERO tenders or contracts containing 'bankomat'/'ATM' in either Cyrillic or Latin, in any year. CPV 30123xxx (cash-handling/coin machines) returns zero; CPV 30132200 (banknote counting machines) returns only four procedures since 09/2025 (Posta 34/2026 and 211/2025, Uprava za trezor OP 3/2026, Putevi Srbije JN 65/2025). No Serbian commercial bank appears as a contracting authority.
signals.source_name: Portal javnih nabavki (UJN) – full-index search via the portal's own searchgrid API
signals.implies: ATM procurement in Serbia does not pass through public procurement at all - it sits with commercial banks and with Postanska stedionica's own website. Agent effort on Serbian ATM opportunities should be redirected to bank-owned procurement pages, not the portal.
signals.followup: Maintain the bank-page watchlist (posted.co.rs plus the commercial banks) as the Serbian ATM channel; use the portal only for NBS, Posta, Treasury and municipal cash/self-service lines.

coverage_notes: Fresh run (no checkpoint existed). Primary-source-first. The portal is an ASP.NET app whose public grids are served by an undocumented JSON API; I reverse-engineered it rather than scraping HTML: GET https://jnportal.ujn.gov.rs/api/searchgrid/<GridName>/get with DevExtreme skip/take/filter/sort params, an anonymous session cookie from any public page, plus a 'UserToken' header taken from the hidden input #uiUserToken on that page. Grids used: TenderNotices (751,942 notices), TendersAll (270,521 procedures), VContracts (395,201 contracts, with winner name + tax ID + value), VAwardDecisions (476,184 award decisions), VProcPlanPublicSearch (24,482 procurement plans). Documents download via /GetDocument.ashx?id=<DmsId>&userToken=<tok>; stable public per-procedure page is /tender-eo/<TenderId>. Searched in Serbian Cyrillic (the portal stores Latin input transliterated, so Latin-only searches under-return) across >30 term variants - bankomat, brojanje/brojac, sorter/sortiranje, novcanica, kovanica, samousluzni, kiosk, POS terminal, platne kartice, ekvajring, HSM, kriptografski, biometrija, identifikacija, pranje novca, transport/prenos novca, gotovina, fizicko-tehnicko obezbedjenje, DinaCard, Cortex, IPS - plus CPV sweeps on 30132xxx, 30123xxx, 66110000, 48810000, 72910xxx. Downloaded and parsed the NBS 2026 procurement plan version 8 (xlsx, 402 rows, adopted 22/07/2026) to status plan lines 0003, 0131, 0132, 0236 against the live procedure list, and to surface seven previously-unreported lines. Cross-checked the Postanska stedionica question directly against the bank's own page. GENUINE GAPS: (1) estimated values are withheld by NBS on essentially every notice, so most NBS opportunities are Unscoped; (2) the Putevi Srbije JN 65/2025 case shows an award decision to Master Team but a discontinued procedure and no contract - I did not open the underlying F03 PDF text to resolve which happened, flagged as follow-up; (3) I did not enumerate every earlier version of the NBS plan, so I cannot say which of the seven newly-surfaced lines were added in v8 versus carried from v1; (4) Serbian commercial banks are structurally absent from the portal and were only partially covered here via posted.co.rs.
access_issues: jnportal.ujn.gov.rs/api/* returns 401 without a session cookie and 403 with a cookie but no UserToken header - both are silent-failure traps; documented the working route above. posted.co.rs, logged as blocked in the baseline, fetched fine (HTTP 200, 57 KB) once a desktop Chrome User-Agent was sent - the block was User-Agent based, not IP based. No PDF extraction was needed: the plan came as xlsx and was parsed locally with Python's zipfile/ElementTree. Claude-in-Chrome was not required. No source was dropped.
